subject: Cashflow horizon proposal + tax routing checklist (TheraHealth)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@therahealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed cashflow horizon and tax routing checklist (TheraHealth)

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. I pulled together a short proposal to close the gap between your procurement timeline and our standard terms so the pilot can go live without a lengthy finance hand-off. High level:

- Proposed payment window: Net 45 for recurring invoices, with a 20% prepayment at PO for the first 30 days to cover onboarding and initial reservation of capacity.
- Conditional credit corridor: We can set an initial credit ceiling of $150k (review after 60 days based on usage and payment cadence).
- VAT/tax routing: For EU invoicing please confirm whether Ther aHealth will accept invoices to the Irish subsidiary (TheraHealth EMEA VAT: IE1234567) or require invoicing to the local EU entity. If you need us to issue invoices with reverse-charge notes, we’ll need a copy of your VAT registration for the receiving entity.

I attached a one-page cashflow schedule (20261119-Proposed-Cashflow-Horizon.xlsx) and a short checklist for VAT evidence. If you’re ok with Net45 + 20% PO prepay, we can produce an amended SOW and invoice the prepay immediately to start provisioning.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm the remit entity for EU VAT and supply the VAT certificate;
2) I share a draft order amendment and the PO line items for prepayment;
3) Finance ops sign-off within 48 hours to avoid losing the onboarding slot.

If you’d prefer Net30 with a smaller prepay instead, we can run the numbers — we want to be flexible, just need clarity on the credit limit and VAT entity.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0144

Attachment: 20261119-Proposed-Cashflow-Horizon.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@therahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts@therahealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Proposed cashflow horizon and tax routing checklist (TheraHealth)

Hi Mina,

Appreciate the clear proposal. A couple items from our side:

- Our procurement team prefers Net30 for pilot engagements; shifting to Net45 will need VP approval.
- We can do the 20% PO prepayment but prefer it to be applied as a credit against the first two invoices rather than a separate prepay line item.
- VAT: For the pilot, invoices should go to Ther aHealth Ltd. (UK entity) — VAT number GB7654321. We can provide the VAT certificate, but note that we still need the invoices to show the local entity for internal accounting.

One more ask: what credit limit would Redwood require to allow Net30 with the modified prepay-credit approach? Our Treasury is sensitive to large upfront vendor credits.

If you can outline the fallback (e.g., automatic downgrade to Net45 or stricter credit ceiling) that helps get this approved quickly.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Senior Procurement Manager
TheraHealth Inc.

Attachment: Ther aHealth-UK-VAT-Certificate.pdf (will send separately)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed cashflow horizon and tax routing checklist (TheraHealth)

Dan —

Thanks for the quick reply and the VAT entity confirmation. To answer your credit question, here’s a pragmatic path that balances your Treasury’s concerns and lets the pilot start on Net30:

- Trial credit ceiling: $75,000 for first 45 days when Net30 is applied.
- Prepay-credit application: the 20% PO prepayment will be posted as an account credit and automatically offset against Invoice #1 and Invoice #2 (we’ll show it as credit memos).
- Review trigger: if invoices are paid within Net30 for the first two billing cycles and utilization stays within forecast, we’ll increase the corridor to $150,000 and keep Net30. If a payment is late beyond 15 days, we revert to Net45 and require a 25% prepayment on new orders until the account is back in good standing.

We’ll also include a short clause in the order amendment that permits Redwood to issue invoices to the UK entity while routing VAT evidence to your Irish or UK VAT number as needed. Please attach the VAT certificate when you have it — that allows us to mark the invoices correctly and avoid reverse-charge disputes.

I’m copying Karthik (sales) to confirm this aligns with the commercial terms you discussed on the demo. Vanessa, Marissa — please confirm the invoice flow and whether the credit memo approach works operationally. If everyone agrees, I’ll drop a branded order amendment and a PO-ready invoice for the 20% prepay this afternoon.

Best,
Mina

Hi Daniel —

Karthik here from the account team. Quick note: the Net30 path with the $75k initial credit corridor looks reasonable to me and should be fine commercially for the pilot. Two operational clarifications:

1) Can Procurement include a PO line called "Onboarding credit" for the 20% so Treasury has a clear ledger line (this avoids confusion in reconciliation). We can still post it as a credit memo internally, but PO visibility helps.
2) Please confirm the expected monthly consumption range so we can calibrate the $75k ceiling. If you expect bursts > $40k in a month, let me know — we may need a short-term surge clause (paid overage) or a larger prepay.

If those two items are ok, I support Mina moving forward with the amendment and the prepay invoice.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Mina / Karthik —

This works for us. A few confirmations before I route to Treasury for final sign-off:

- We will raise a PO with an "Onboarding credit" line for 20% (expected amount ~ $9,600) and note the credit application against Invoice 001/002.
- We accept the $75k initial credit corridor with the 60-day review cadence.
- VAT certificate attached here (TheraHealth-UK-VAT-Certificate.pdf). Please use the UK entity on the invoices.

Mina — please send the order amendment and the PO-ready invoice and I’ll push this to Treasury. If Treasury needs a short note from Redwood (one paragraph) explaining the downgrade trigger (Net45 on late payment) and the credit ceiling mechanics, I can include it in the submission.

Thanks,
Daniel
